2025-26.title: OptiQomm
2025-26.author: Horizon Instrumentation Team
2025-26.excerpt: OptiQomm aims to develop a portable optical ground station for tracking LEO satellites and establishing optical links for quantum communication. The project combines precision satellite tracking, optics, and quantum key distribution to explore secure satellite-to-ground communication.
2025-26.content:
Overview

OptiQomm is developing a portable optical ground station for tracking LEO satellites, with the goal of establishing optical and quantum links for Quantum Key Distribution (QKD).

Motivation

  • Develop a portable system capable of accurately tracking LEO satellites.
  • Establish reliable optical links for quantum communication and secure key distribution.
  • Explore the challenges of satellite-to-ground quantum communication, including atmospheric effects.

Method

  • Satellite Tracking: Use a dual-layer tracking algorithm, combining open-loop TLE-based tracking with closed-loop image tracking for high-precision pointing.
  • Optical System: Employ a motorized equatorial mount with wide- and narrow-field-of-view cameras for coarse and fine tracking, supported by Kalman filtering.
  • Quantum Communication: Implement the BB84 protocol and study photon detection, time-tagging, and time-multiplexing techniques.
  • Optical Setup: Develop a Quantum Transmitter/"Alice Station" and study atmospheric effects such as scintillation to optimize communication performance.

Results

  • Successfully developed and tested the satellite tracking system, including custom firmware and ASCOM-compatible software.
  • Captured the image of a satellite using the in-house telescope and tracking setup.
  • Finalized the BB84 protocol implementation and established the initial optical setup for quantum links.
  • Evaluated quantum bit error rates and secure key rates using atmospheric models.

Future Improvements

  • Integrate a 3D-printed galvohead scanner and mirror-steering system for improved beam pointing.
  • Implement real-time modelling of atmospheric scintillation to optimize communication performance.
  • Successfully track satellites and establish quantum links in future experiments.
  • Develop a single-photon detection system using Avalanche Photodiodes (APDs) and build a single-photon source for the setup.

2025-26.title: Radian
2025-26.author: Horizon Instrumentation Team
2025-26.excerpt: Aims to mitigate radio-frequency interference and recover faint astronomical signals such as the 21 cm hydrogen line using specialized antennas and signal-processing techniques.
2025-26.content:
Overview

The RADIAN Project aims to mitigate Radio Frequency Interference (RFI)—unwanted man-made radio signals that often overpower the faint radio waves arriving from space. The project's primary goal is to detect the 21 cm hydrogen line (1420 MHz), an important astronomical signal emitted by neutral hydrogen. Although this frequency is protected for radio astronomy, interference from satellites, radar systems, mobile communications, and even the instrument itself makes detection extremely challenging.

Motivation

  • Detect the faint 21 cm hydrogen line, which is crucial for radio astronomy
  • Remove artificial radio signals that obscure valuable astronomical data
  • Improve the quality of observations for studying the Universe

Method

Data Collection: Use a Log-Periodic Dipole Antenna (LPDA) to collect radio signals over a wide range of frequencies with an improved signal-to-noise ratio.

Spectrogram Generation: Convert the raw data into a spectrogram to analyze signal power across time and frequency.

Noise Removal: Apply edge detection and baseline fitting to identify RFI and remove background noise generated by the instrument.

RFI Detection: Identify interference patterns such as bursts, broadband noise, and narrowband signals using algorithms like the Sum-Threshold method.

Results

  • Successfully detects and flags several common forms of radio frequency interference
  • Produces cleaner radio astronomy data while preserving the underlying astronomical signal
  • Faces challenges due to the large memory requirements of processing radio data and the risk of accidentally removing weak cosmic signals

Future Improvements

  • Develop machine learning models to automatically classify different types of RFI
  • Improve interference removal while preserving faint astronomical signals
  • Enhance the pipeline to achieve reliable detection of the 21 cm hydrogen line

2025-26.title: StarSpec
2025-26.author: Horizon Instrumentation Team
2025-26.excerpt: Uses spectroscopy to study the Sun and distant stars, extracting information about their composition, temperature, motion, and other physical properties through their spectra.
2025-26.content:
Overview

StarSpec is a spectroscopy project dedicated to studying the Sun, stars, and planets by analyzing the light they emit. Spectroscopy allows astronomers to determine properties such as temperature, chemical composition, motion, and luminosity, making it one of the most powerful tools for understanding celestial objects.

Motivation

  • Use spectroscopy to uncover the physical properties of stars, planets, and the Sun
  • Gain hands-on experience by designing, building, and operating spectrographs
  • Explore how light can reveal information hidden across the cosmos

Method

Solar Spectroscopy (Sol'Ex): Use the Solar Explorer (Sol'Ex) spectrograph to observe sunspots, solar flares, and the solar atmosphere.

Spectrum Formation: Sunlight passes through a 10 µm slit, is collimated, dispersed by a 2400 lines/mm diffraction grating, and focused onto a detector to produce a spectrum.

Data Analysis: Analyze the recorded spectra using SpecINTI, calibrated with a neon lamp spectrum, to measure properties such as solar flare velocities through the Doppler effect.

Stellar Spectroscopy (Star'Ex): A modified version of Sol'Ex with a 100 lines/mm diffraction grating and a guiding module enables observations of distant stars by improving light collection and maintaining accurate tracking.

Results

  • Successfully captures and analyzes spectra from the Sun, bright stars, and planets
  • Extracts valuable information such as temperature, chemical composition, luminosity, and motion from observed spectra
  • Demonstrates the effectiveness of custom-built spectrographs for both solar and stellar observations

Future Improvements

  • Build more advanced, in-house spectroscopy instruments, including the UVEX (UltraViolet EXplorer)
  • Conduct new studies such as measuring galaxy redshifts, detecting supernovae, and monitoring the time evolution of hydrogen spectral lines
  • Expand collaborative research through participation in the AAVSOnet Telescope Spectroscopy Working Group and contribute to the development of a dedicated spectroscopy telescope

2025-26.title: LIGO
2025-26.author: Horizon Instrumentation Team
2025-26.excerpt: A university-scale gravitational-wave detector prototype inspired by LIGO-India, focusing on precision interferometry, vibration isolation, suspended mirrors, and advanced sensing and control systems.
2025-26.content:
Overview

The LIGO Prototype Project at Horizon is inspired by the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO), which detects gravitational waves—tiny ripples in spacetime produced by massive accelerating objects such as merging black holes. These waves cause incredibly small distortions in space, making their detection one of the most precise experimental achievements in modern physics.

Motivation

  • Understand the principles behind gravitational wave detection and interferometry
  • Build a university-scale prototype inspired by LIGO-India
  • Gain practical experience in precision optics, vibration isolation, control systems, and instrumentation

Method

Interferometry: Use a Michelson interferometer where laser beams travel through perpendicular arms, reflect from mirrors, and recombine to detect minute changes in path length.

Vibration Isolation: Suspend mirrors with multi-degree-of-freedom mechanical systems and electromagnetic actuators to minimize external disturbances.

Precision Components: Integrate ultra-stable lasers, mechanical suspensions, PID controllers, transimpedance amplifiers, piezoelectric transducers, and Optical Sensor and Electromagnet Modules (OSEMs) for sensing and actuation.

Software & Modeling: Develop optics simulations, suspension models, and electrical systems to improve signal-to-noise ratio and validate experimental performance.

Results

  • Successfully developed a university-scale LIGO prototype over two years under the LIGO-India initiative
  • Established vibration isolation and mirror suspension systems for precision interferometry
  • Demonstrated integration of optical, mechanical, electronic, and software subsystems toward gravitational wave detection principles

Future Improvements

  • Complete the integration of all hardware and software subsystems into a fully functional prototype
  • Improve performance through mode locking, band-pass filtering, and modal damping techniques
  • Demonstrate a working interferometer capable of showcasing the core principles behind gravitational wave detection

2026-27.title: Sonicphase
2026-27.author: Horizon Instrumentation Team
2026-27.excerpt: An innovative project exploring advancements in sonic phase manipulation.
2026-27.content:
Overview

Sonicphase investigates new methods for controlling and manipulating sound waves through phase modulation.

This research could lead to applications in acoustics, noise cancellation, and ultrasonic imaging.

2026-27.title: Quantaband
2026-27.author: Horizon Instrumentation Team
2026-27.excerpt: A project focused on quantum bandgap engineering for advanced materials.
2026-27.content:
Overview

Quantaband explores the principles of quantum mechanics to engineer the bandgaps of novel materials.

This work has potential applications in semiconductor technology and quantum computing.

2026-27.title: Ferrostats
2026-27.author: Horizon Instrumentation Team
2026-27.excerpt: Development of ferroelectric statistical models for advanced device applications.
2026-27.content:
Overview

Ferrostats focuses on developing sophisticated statistical models for ferroelectric materials.

These models are crucial for designing next-generation electronic devices that utilize ferroelectric properties.
